dataFlows.transformKql:
source
| where type == "indicator" and pattern_type == "stix" and isnotempty(pattern)
| extend TimeGenerated = now()
| extend Pattern = tostring(pattern)
| extend PatternVersion = tostring(pattern_version)
| extend SourceStixId = tostring(id)
| extend idHex = substring(tostring(hash_sha256(strcat(SourceStixId, '|', Pattern))), 0, 32)
| extend Id = strcat('indicator--', substring(idHex,0,8), '-', substring(idHex,8,4), '-', substring(idHex,12,4), '-', substring(idHex,16,4), '-', substring(idHex,20,12))
| extend ValidFromRaw = tostring(valid_from)
| extend ConfidenceRaw = toint(confidence)
| extend CreatedRaw = tostring(created)
| extend ModifiedRaw = tostring(modified)
| extend ParsedKey = extract(@"^\[(.*?) = '", 1, Pattern)
| extend ParsedValueRaw = extract(@"= '(.*)'\]$", 1, Pattern)
| extend UnescapeStep1 = replace(@"\\\\", "@@BKSL@@", ParsedValueRaw)
| extend UnescapeStep2 = replace(@"\\'", "'", UnescapeStep1)
| extend ParsedValue = replace("@@BKSL@@", @"\\", UnescapeStep2)
| extend ObservableKey = iff(isempty(ParsedKey), "stix:pattern", ParsedKey)
| extend ObservableValue = iff(isempty(ParsedKey), Pattern, ParsedValue)
| extend SourceSystem = 'PolySwarm'
| extend LastUpdateMethod = 'PolySwarm curated feed'
| extend Confidence = ConfidenceRaw
| extend IsActive = true
| extend IsDeleted = false
| extend Revoked = false
| extend ValidFrom = todatetime(ValidFromRaw)
| extend ValidUntil = datetime_add('day', 90, todatetime(ValidFromRaw))
| extend Created = todatetime(CreatedRaw)
| extend Modified = todatetime(ModifiedRaw)
| extend AdditionalFields = pack('source_stix_id', SourceStixId, 'pattern_version', PatternVersion, 'observable_parse_note', iff(isempty(ParsedKey), 'pattern did not match the expected [key = value] STIX comparison shape; Pattern and Data are still authoritative, only ObservableKey and ObservableValue are best effort', ''))
| extend Data = pack('type', 'indicator', 'spec_version', '2.1', 'id', Id, 'created', CreatedRaw, 'modified', ModifiedRaw, 'pattern', Pattern, 'pattern_type', 'stix', 'pattern_version', PatternVersion, 'valid_from', ValidFromRaw, 'confidence', Confidence, 'indicator_types', pack_array('malicious-activity'))
| project TimeGenerated, Id, ObservableKey, ObservableValue, Pattern, SourceSystem, Confidence, IsActive, IsDeleted, Revoked, ValidFrom, ValidUntil, Created, Modified, LastUpdateMethod, AdditionalFields, Data

properties.description:
Any PolySwarm hunting connector hit (ThreatIntelIndicators, SourceSystem "PolySwarm", with a hunt rule name) with
Confidence at or above 90 created in the last hour, grouped by malware family. Each hunt hit is counted once, on its SHA-256 indicator
(the SHA-1 and MD5 indicators of the same hit are skipped).
Confidence carries the PolyScore for the sample. Family and rule name come from
AdditionalFields.
properties.query:
ThreatIntelIndicators
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where SourceSystem == "PolySwarm"
| where Confidence >= 90
| where isnotempty(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).rule_name))
| where IsActive and (isempty(ValidUntil) or ValidUntil > now())
| where ObservableKey has "file:hashes"
| where tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).digest_type) == "SHA-256"
| extend FileHashValue = ObservableValue
| extend HashAlgorithm = case(ObservableKey has "SHA-256", "SHA256", ObservableKey has "SHA-1", "SHA1", ObservableKey has "MD5", "MD5", "")
| extend Family = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).family)
| extend RuleName = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).rule_name)
| extend Community = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).community)
| extend Permalink = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).permalink)
| extend Detections = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).detections)
| summarize HitCount = count(), TimeGenerated = arg_max(TimeGenerated, Permalink, Detections) by Id, FileHashValue, HashAlgorithm, Family, RuleName, Community, Confidence
| project TimeGenerated, FileHashValue, HashAlgorithm, Family, RuleName, Community, Confidence, Permalink, Detections, HitCount

properties.description:
Matches PolySwarm file-hash indicators (from live hunt results and the curated feed,
both landing in ThreatIntelIndicators with SourceSystem "PolySwarm") against
DeviceFileEvents, DeviceProcessEvents, SecurityEvent and CommonSecurityLog on SHA-256, SHA-1 and MD5 (both sides lowercased). The alert carries
the evidence: PolyScore, detection counts, malware family, hunt rule and report link.
properties.query:
let dt_lookBack = 1h;
let ioc_lookBack = 14d;
let PolySwarmHashes = ThreatIntelIndicators
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(ioc_lookBack)
    | where SourceSystem == "PolySwarm"
    | where ObservableKey in ("file:hashes.'SHA-256'", "file:hashes.SHA-256", "file:hashes.'SHA-1'", "file:hashes.SHA-1", "file:hashes.'MD5'", "file:hashes.MD5")
    | where isnotempty(ObservableValue)
    | summarize LatestIndicatorTime = arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Id
    | where IsActive and (isempty(ValidUntil) or ValidUntil > now())
    | extend FileHashValue = tolower(ObservableValue)
    | extend HashAlgorithm = case(ObservableKey has "SHA-256", "SHA256", ObservableKey has "SHA-1", "SHA1", "MD5")
    | extend Family = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).family)
    | extend RuleName = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).rule_name)
    | extend PolyScore = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).polyscore)
    | extend DetectionsMalicious = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).detections.malicious)
    | extend DetectionsTotal = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).detections.total)
    | extend Permalink = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).permalink);
let DeviceHashEvents = union
    (DeviceFileEvents
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(dt_lookBack)
      | extend HostName = DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, EventTime = TimeGenerated
      | extend HashList = pack_array(tolower(SHA256), tolower(SHA1), tolower(MD5))
      | mv-expand FileHashValue = HashList to typeof(string)
      | where isnotempty(FileHashValue)),
    (DeviceProcessEvents
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(dt_lookBack)
      | extend HostName = DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, EventTime = TimeGenerated
      | extend HashList = pack_array(tolower(SHA256), tolower(SHA1), tolower(MD5))
      | mv-expand FileHashValue = HashList to typeof(string)
      | where isnotempty(FileHashValue));
let SecurityEventHashEvents = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(dt_lookBack)
    | where isnotempty(FileHash)
    | extend FileHashValue = tolower(FileHash), HostName = Computer, AccountName = Account, EventTime = TimeGenerated;
let CommonSecurityLogHashEvents = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(dt_lookBack)
    | where isnotempty(FileHash)

metadata.description: Takes every FileHash entity on a Microsoft Sentinel incident, looks it up in the PolySwarm REST API v3, and writes a verdict / PolyScore / engine / malware-family / sandbox / ATT&CK summary back to the incident as a comment.
prerequisites: A PolySwarm API key with access to the target community, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault. Get a key at https://polyswarm.network/account/api-keys

postDeployment: 1. Grant this playbook's system-assigned managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault named in KeyVaultName.
2. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's system-assigned managed identity.
3. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel and Key Vault API connections if they show as unauthorized.
4. Attach the playbook to an automation rule so it runs when an incident is created.

metadata.title: PolySwarm - URL Enrichment - Incident Triggered
metadata.description: Takes every URL entity on a Microsoft Sentinel incident, looks it up in the PolySwarm REST API v3, and writes a PolyScore, engine, DNS and TLS certificate summary back to the incident as a comment.
prerequisites: A PolySwarm API key with access to the target community, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault. Get a key at https://polyswarm.network/account/api-keys
postDeployment: 1. Grant this playbook's system-assigned managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault named in KeyVaultName.
2. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's system-assigned managed identity.
3. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel and Key Vault API connections if they show as unauthorized.
4. Attach the playbook to an automation rule so it runs when an incident is created.

metadata.description: Name of the Logic App playbook resource.
Version string sent in the User-Agent header on every call to the PolySwarm API. Bump this when the solution version changes.

PolySwarm sandbox community slug to detonate into. No default value on purpose: this playbook refuses to fall back to the public 'default' community silently. Pass your private community slug. To explicitly submit into the public community instead, also set AllowPublicCommunity to true.
Must be explicitly set to true to allow Community to resolve to 'default' (the public community). A file pulled off an endpoint and detonated publicly becomes public. Leave false unless you mean it.

PolySwarm sandbox provider_slug: 'triage' or 'cape'. Live-verified 2026-09-23: both providers auto-extract a gzip archive and analyze the inner file, so this playbook submits the file straight from Defender still gzip-compressed (as a .gz) with no in-workflow decompression, and either provider is a valid choice; no restriction. See GET /v3/sandbox/provider/list for the live slug list.

PolySwarm sandbox vm_slug (VM image) to detonate in; must be a VM the chosen Provider actually offers. Live-checked against GET /v3/sandbox/provider/list on 2026-09-23: triage offers windows11-21h2-x64, ubuntu-22.04-amd64, android-11-x64; cape offers only win-10-build-19041. The default here (windows11-21h2-x64) matches the default Provider (triage); switching Provider to 'cape' requires also setting this to 'win-10-build-19041', they are not interchangeable across providers.
Whether the sandbox VM has outbound network access during detonation.

Minutes to wait for the Defender live response action AND, separately, for the PolySwarm sandbox task, before giving up and commenting a timeout. Applied independently to each of the two polling loops.
Name of the Azure Key Vault holding the PolySwarm API key secret. Grant this playbook's managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the vault after deployment.
Name of the secret in Key Vault holding the PolySwarm API key, sent verbatim as the Authorization header (no 'Bearer ' prefix).

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint API base URL. Also used as the OAuth audience for the managed identity token, which must match the resource the WindowsDefenderATP app roles were granted against -- see grant-defender-permissions.sh. Do not change this to api.security.microsoft.com without also re-pointing the audience and re-checking the app role grant; see the playbook README.
PolySwarm REST API v3 base URL.

Files larger than this (measured on the gzip-compressed bytes Defender returns, which this playbook submits to PolySwarm as-is) are not downloaded; the playbook comments the Defender live response download link instead (valid 30 minutes) rather than attempt a transfer that will fail. Default 104857600 (100 MB) is the documented Logic Apps HTTP message-size ceiling without chunking; with chunking enabled (as this playbook's HTTP actions request) Logic Apps allows up to 1 GB per action in practice, and Defender's own getfile ceiling is 3 GB, but neither of those higher numbers has been live-tested here -- raise this only after confirming chunking actually works end to end.

Sandbox report score (0-10 scale, coalesce(report.malscore, report.analysis.score)) at or above which the incident comment and PolySwarmSandbox_CL row report Verdict 'malicious'. Calibrated against a known LockBit sample (CAPE malscore 8.0, Triage analysis.score 10).

Sandbox report score at or above which (and below MaliciousScoreThreshold) Verdict is 'suspicious'. Below this, Verdict is 'benign'. A null score reports 'unknown'; a sandbox task status of KNOWN_GOOD reports 'known good' regardless of score.

Logs ingestion URL of the Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) that fronts the PolySwarmSandbox_CL Data Collection Rule, e.g. https://<dce-name>-<suffix>.<region>-1.ingest.monitor.azure.com. No default: workspace-specific, matches the shared DCE/DCR template's dceLogsIngestionEndpoint output.

Immutable ID (dcr-...) of the Data Collection Rule that accepts PolySwarmSandbox_CL rows, used in the Logs Ingestion API URL path. No default: workspace-specific, matches the shared DCE/DCR template's dcrImmutableId output. This is NOT the same value as DcrResourceId below -- see that parameter.
Custom stream name on the Data Collection Rule that maps incoming rows to the PolySwarmSandbox_CL table. Matches the shared DCE/DCR template's streamName output.

Full ARM resource ID of the same Data Collection Rule identified by dcrImmutableId above (/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules/<name>). A DCR's immutableId and its ARM resource ID are two different identifiers; the Logs Ingestion API URL needs the former, and the role assignment below (scope) needs the latter. No default: workspace-specific.

If true, this template automatically assigns the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role on DcrResourceId to this playbook's managed identity. Same pattern as Recorded Future's sandbox playbooks. Set false and grant it manually (see grant-defender-permissions.sh --help) if this identity does not have rights to create role assignments at deployment time.

If true (default), sends an Office 365 Outlook approval email to ApproverEmail before retrieving any file from a device with Defender live response, and only proceeds to GetFile if the approver clicks Approve within ApprovalTimeoutHours. Protects against the residual risk of someone placing the genuine hash of a sensitive file on an incident to have this playbook exfiltrate it. Set false only if another control in your environment covers this risk.

Email address the approval request is sent to when RequireAnalystApproval is true. Required in that case. The Office 365 Outlook connection (authorized post-deployment, see README) sends the approval request from its own signed-in mailbox to this address.
Hours to wait for the analyst's approval response before treating the request as a timeout and stopping without retrieving the file. Only applies when RequireAnalystApproval is true.

Case-insensitive substrings checked against the full retrieved file path (Defender's FolderPath, which already includes the file name). Defaults cover common browser credential stores, the Windows credential/DPAPI/vault stores, the SAM/SYSTEM hives under System32\config, NTDS.dit, KeePass databases and SSH private keys. A match stops the playbook before Defender live response GetFile runs, with an incident comment -- checked before the approval email is sent, and even when RequireAnalystApproval would otherwise have allowed it through.

metadata.title: PolySwarm - Sandbox Defender File Detonation - Entity Triggered (Preview)
metadata.description: Preview: deploys and passes every local check, but has not yet been run against a live Defender for Endpoint tenant. Feedback to support@polyswarm.io. Starting from a Microsoft Sentinel FileHash entity, runs a Defender for Endpoint advanced hunting query to find where a SHA256 was last seen, pulls the file off that device with Defender live response (GetFile), and submits it to the PolySwarm sandbox (private community by default) for detonation. Comments the verdict, score, family, ATT&CK techniques and report link back on the incident. Companion to the incident-triggered variant in this same folder.
prerequisites: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, with live response and live response for servers enabled under Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features.
A PolySwarm API key with sandbox access to a private community, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault this subscription can reach.
A SHA256-only flow: this playbook skips MD5/SHA1 FileHash entities, since Defender's DeviceFileEvents/DeviceProcessEvents are indexed on SHA256.
postDeployment: 1. Grant this playbook's system-assigned managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault named in KeyVaultName.

2. Run grant-defender-permissions.sh (in this folder) against the resource group, passing this playbook's name, to grant Machine.LiveResponse, Machine.ReadWrite.All and AdvancedQuery.Read.All on the WindowsDefenderATP API to the managed identity. NOTE: this is Machine.ReadWrite.All, not Machine.Read.All -- see README, 'A permission correction'.
3. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel and Key Vault API connections if they show as unauthorized.
4. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's managed identity so it can comment on incidents.

5. This template auto-assigns 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' on DcrResourceId to the managed identity when create_role_assignment is true (default). If deployed with create_role_assignment=false, grant it manually the same way as the Key Vault role in step 1, scoped to the DCR resource instead -- grant-defender-permissions.sh does not do this (it is an Azure RBAC role assignment, not a WindowsDefenderATP application permission).
6. Attach to an automation rule scoped to FileHash entities.

metadata.description: Name of the Logic App playbook resource.
Version string sent in the User-Agent header on every call to the PolySwarm API. Bump this when the solution version changes.

PolySwarm sandbox community slug to detonate into. No default value on purpose: this playbook refuses to fall back to the public 'default' community silently. Pass your private community slug. To explicitly submit into the public community instead, also set AllowPublicCommunity to true.
Must be explicitly set to true to allow Community to resolve to 'default' (the public community). A file pulled off an endpoint and detonated publicly becomes public. Leave false unless you mean it.

PolySwarm sandbox provider_slug: 'triage' or 'cape'. Live-verified 2026-09-23: both providers auto-extract a gzip archive and analyze the inner file, so this playbook submits the file straight from Defender still gzip-compressed (as a .gz) with no in-workflow decompression, and either provider is a valid choice; no restriction. See GET /v3/sandbox/provider/list for the live slug list.

PolySwarm sandbox vm_slug (VM image) to detonate in; must be a VM the chosen Provider actually offers. Live-checked against GET /v3/sandbox/provider/list on 2026-09-23: triage offers windows11-21h2-x64, ubuntu-22.04-amd64, android-11-x64; cape offers only win-10-build-19041. The default here (windows11-21h2-x64) matches the default Provider (triage); switching Provider to 'cape' requires also setting this to 'win-10-build-19041', they are not interchangeable across providers.
Whether the sandbox VM has outbound network access during detonation.

Minutes to wait for the Defender live response action AND, separately, for the PolySwarm sandbox task, before giving up and commenting a timeout. Applied independently to each of the two polling loops.
Name of the Azure Key Vault holding the PolySwarm API key secret. Grant this playbook's managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the vault after deployment.
Name of the secret in Key Vault holding the PolySwarm API key, sent verbatim as the Authorization header (no 'Bearer ' prefix).

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint API base URL. Also used as the OAuth audience for the managed identity token, which must match the resource the WindowsDefenderATP app roles were granted against -- see grant-defender-permissions.sh. Do not change this to api.security.microsoft.com without also re-pointing the audience and re-checking the app role grant; see the playbook README.
PolySwarm REST API v3 base URL.

Files larger than this (measured on the gzip-compressed bytes Defender returns, which this playbook submits to PolySwarm as-is) are not downloaded; the playbook comments the Defender live response download link instead (valid 30 minutes) rather than attempt a transfer that will fail. Default 104857600 (100 MB) is the documented Logic Apps HTTP message-size ceiling without chunking; with chunking enabled (as this playbook's HTTP actions request) Logic Apps allows up to 1 GB per action in practice, and Defender's own getfile ceiling is 3 GB, but neither of those higher numbers has been live-tested here -- raise this only after confirming chunking actually works end to end.

Sandbox report score (0-10 scale, coalesce(report.malscore, report.analysis.score)) at or above which the incident comment and PolySwarmSandbox_CL row report Verdict 'malicious'. Calibrated against a known LockBit sample (CAPE malscore 8.0, Triage analysis.score 10).

Sandbox report score at or above which (and below MaliciousScoreThreshold) Verdict is 'suspicious'. Below this, Verdict is 'benign'. A null score reports 'unknown'; a sandbox task status of KNOWN_GOOD reports 'known good' regardless of score.

Logs ingestion URL of the Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) that fronts the PolySwarmSandbox_CL Data Collection Rule, e.g. https://<dce-name>-<suffix>.<region>-1.ingest.monitor.azure.com. No default: workspace-specific, matches the shared DCE/DCR template's dceLogsIngestionEndpoint output.

Immutable ID (dcr-...) of the Data Collection Rule that accepts PolySwarmSandbox_CL rows, used in the Logs Ingestion API URL path. No default: workspace-specific, matches the shared DCE/DCR template's dcrImmutableId output. This is NOT the same value as DcrResourceId below -- see that parameter.
Custom stream name on the Data Collection Rule that maps incoming rows to the PolySwarmSandbox_CL table. Matches the shared DCE/DCR template's streamName output.

Full ARM resource ID of the same Data Collection Rule identified by dcrImmutableId above (/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules/<name>). A DCR's immutableId and its ARM resource ID are two different identifiers; the Logs Ingestion API URL needs the former, and the role assignment below (scope) needs the latter. No default: workspace-specific.

If true, this template automatically assigns the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role on DcrResourceId to this playbook's managed identity. Same pattern as Recorded Future's sandbox playbooks. Set false and grant it manually (see grant-defender-permissions.sh --help) if this identity does not have rights to create role assignments at deployment time.

If true (default), sends an Office 365 Outlook approval email to ApproverEmail before retrieving any file from a device with Defender live response, and only proceeds to GetFile if the approver clicks Approve within ApprovalTimeoutHours. Protects against the residual risk of someone placing the genuine hash of a sensitive file on an incident to have this playbook exfiltrate it. Set false only if another control in your environment covers this risk.

Email address the approval request is sent to when RequireAnalystApproval is true. Required in that case. The Office 365 Outlook connection (authorized post-deployment, see README) sends the approval request from its own signed-in mailbox to this address.
Hours to wait for the analyst's approval response before treating the request as a timeout and stopping without retrieving the file. Only applies when RequireAnalystApproval is true.

Case-insensitive substrings checked against the full retrieved file path (Defender's FolderPath, which already includes the file name). Defaults cover common browser credential stores, the Windows credential/DPAPI/vault stores, the SAM/SYSTEM hives under System32\config, NTDS.dit, KeePass databases and SSH private keys. A match stops the playbook before Defender live response GetFile runs, with an incident comment -- checked before the approval email is sent, and even when RequireAnalystApproval would otherwise have allowed it through.

metadata.title: PolySwarm - Sandbox Defender File Detonation - Incident Triggered (Preview)
metadata.description: Preview: deploys and passes every local check, but has not yet been run against a live Defender for Endpoint tenant. Feedback to support@polyswarm.io. Starting from a Microsoft Sentinel incident, runs a Defender for Endpoint advanced hunting query to find where a SHA256 was last seen, pulls the file off that device with Defender live response (GetFile), and submits it to the PolySwarm sandbox (private community by default) for detonation. Comments the verdict, score, family, ATT&CK techniques and report link back on the incident. Companion to the entity-triggered variant in this same folder.
prerequisites: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, with live response and live response for servers enabled under Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features.
A PolySwarm API key with sandbox access to a private community, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault this subscription can reach.
A SHA256-only flow: this playbook skips MD5/SHA1 FileHash entities, since Defender's DeviceFileEvents/DeviceProcessEvents are indexed on SHA256.
postDeployment: 1. Grant this playbook's system-assigned managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault named in KeyVaultName.

2. Run grant-defender-permissions.sh (in this folder) against the resource group, passing this playbook's name, to grant Machine.LiveResponse, Machine.ReadWrite.All and AdvancedQuery.Read.All on the WindowsDefenderATP API to the managed identity. NOTE: this is Machine.ReadWrite.All, not Machine.Read.All -- see README, 'A permission correction'.
3. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel and Key Vault API connections if they show as unauthorized.
4. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's managed identity so it can comment on incidents.

5. This template auto-assigns 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' on DcrResourceId to the managed identity when create_role_assignment is true (default). If deployed with create_role_assignment=false, grant it manually the same way as the Key Vault role in step 1, scoped to the DCR resource instead -- grant-defender-permissions.sh does not do this (it is an Azure RBAC role assignment, not a WindowsDefenderATP application permission).
6. Attach to an automation rule.

Initialize_sandbox_status.description: Top-level initialization required by Logic Apps (InitializeVariable is not allowed inside a scope). Reset to the same value at the point in the loop where the task's real starting status is known - see Reset_sandbox_status.

For_each_mail.description: Runs once per Mail entity on the incident. Gets the message by id with the Office 365 Outlook connector, lists its attachments and detonates each one in the PolySwarm sandbox, then comments the verdict, score, malware family, MITRE ATT&CK techniques and report link on the incident. The playbook never creates incidents.

List_attachments.description: Office 365 Outlook connector, by message id from the Microsoft Sentinel Mail entity (NetworkMessageId / InternetMessageId depending on the entity's populated field - use whichever the entity carries).

For_each_attachment.description: One sandbox submission per attachment on the mail message referenced by the incident's Mail entity.

Get_PolySwarm_API_key.description: Reads the PolySwarm API key from Key Vault via the playbook's managed identity. Never a deployment parameter.

Guard_community_is_not_public_unless_exp.description: Decisions locked #2: sandbox submissions default to the private community; public only by explicit parameter choice. Community has no ARM default (required parameter), and even when set to 'public' or 'default' the submission is refused unless AllowPublicCommunity is explicitly true.

Create_sandbox_task.description: Step 1 of 3, for the current mail attachment.

Upload_artifact_bytes.description: Step 2 of 3. The Office 365 'Get attachment' action below returns ContentBytes as base64; base64ToBinary decodes it before the PUT. No Authorization header - matches the verified upload_file() behaviour.

Finalize_sandbox_task.description: Step 3 of 3. Task id goes in the query string, community in the JSON body.

Reset_sandbox_status.description: Starts this loop iteration's polling clean. InitializeVariable cannot live here (Logic Apps only allows it at the top level of the workflow) - sandboxStatus is initialized once at the top of the workflow and reset to the real starting value here on every iteration.

Set_sandbox_status.description: HTTP 204 with an empty body means PolySwarm has no such task (not found). It is handled explicitly as NOT_FOUND, which ends the poll loop, and the empty body is never read.

Compose_next_sandbox_status.description: Computes the next value of sandboxStatus. Logic Apps does not allow a variable to be set from an expression that reads the same variable.

Build_summary.description: Builds the summary used for both the incident comment and the PolySwarmSandbox_CL row, from the last poll of the sandbox task. The score is on the 0 to 10 scale both sandbox providers use. Verdict rule, used everywhere: KNOWN_GOOD is 'known good'; no score is 'unknown' (this covers a failed task and a timeout); at or above MaliciousScoreThreshold is 'malicious'; at or above SuspiciousScoreThreshold is 'suspicious'; otherwise 'benign'.

Determine_outcome.description: Outcome category, used only to choose the incident comment's narrative text - the verdict value itself (Build_summary?['verdict']) is the same single rule in every branch and in the PolySwarmSandbox_CL row.

Send_to_PolySwarmSandbox_CL.description: Logs Ingestion API: one row per detonation attempt, keyed by TaskId. CompletedAt is this playbook's own observed-terminal timestamp (utcNow()) - the verified SandboxTask response shape has no server-provided completion time.

metadata.title: PolySwarm - Sandbox Outlook Attachment Detonation - Incident Triggered (Preview)
metadata.description: Preview: deploys and passes every local check, but has not yet been run against a live Exchange Online mailbox. Feedback to support@polyswarm.io. For every MailMessage entity on a Microsoft Sentinel incident, retrieves the message's attachments via the Office 365 Outlook connector and detonates each in the PolySwarm sandbox (CAPE or Triage), polling until complete or timeout and commenting verdict, score, malware family, MITRE ATT&CK techniques and a report link back to the incident. Defaults to your private PolySwarm community; refuses to submit to the public community unless AllowPublicCommunity is explicitly set. Never creates an incident.
prerequisites: A PolySwarm API key with sandbox access, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault.
The private PolySwarm community you want detonations to land in.
An Office 365 mailbox connection with permission to read the mail message referenced by the incident's Mail entity.

The PolySwarmSandbox_CL Data Collection Endpoint and Data Collection Rule deployed (Data Connectors folder - not owned by this playbook). This playbook is the only writer to that table: it POSTs one row per detonation attempt (including timeouts) via the Logs Ingestion API, since PolySwarm's own sandbox task list API does not carry verdicts.
postDeployment: 1. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's system-assigned managed identity.
2. Assign the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault (named by the KeyVaultName parameter) to the same managed identity.

3. The 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' role on the Data Collection Rule (DcrResourceId) is assigned automatically at deployment when create_role_assignment is true (default) and the deploying principal can grant RBAC roles on that DCR; otherwise set create_role_assignment to false and assign the role manually.
4. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel, Azure Key Vault and Office 365 API connections if they show as unauthorized.
5. Attach the playbook to an automation rule so it runs on incidents with a Mail entity, or run it manually.

Initialize_sandbox_status.description: Top-level initialization required by Logic Apps (InitializeVariable is not allowed inside a scope). Reset to the same value at the point in the loop where the task's real starting status is known - see Reset_sandbox_status.

For_each_file.description: PolySwarm-Sandbox-StorageBlob differs from the reference playbooks it is modelled on (Recorded Future Sandbox_StorageAccount, Google GTIFileScanBlobEnrichment): those trigger directly off a blob-added event and, having no incident, write to a custom Log Analytics table for an analytics rule to pick up. This playbook is Microsoft Sentinel incident-triggered instead, so it always has an incident to comment on and detonates the exact blob a File entity on the incident names (StorageAccountName/ContainerName are fixed deployment parameters naming where an upstream process - for example a SOAR evidence-capture step - already placed the file; FileName comes from the incident's File entity). Uses the same Azure Blob Storage connector 'get blob content by path' operation the reference playbooks use, just invoked on demand instead of via the 'When a blob is added or modified' trigger.

Get_PolySwarm_API_key.description: Reads the PolySwarm API key from Key Vault via the playbook's managed identity. Never a deployment parameter.

Guard_community_is_not_public_unless_exp.description: Decisions locked #2: sandbox submissions default to the private community; public only by explicit parameter choice. Community has no ARM default (required parameter), and even when set to 'public' or 'default' the submission is refused unless AllowPublicCommunity is explicitly true.

Get_blob_content.description: Azure Blob Storage connector with managed identity authentication. Reads the blob named in the incident's file entity.

Create_sandbox_task.description: Step 1 of 3, for the blob matching the current File entity's FileName inside ContainerName.

Upload_artifact_bytes.description: Step 2 of 3. Body is the raw blob content from Get_blob_content. No Authorization header - matches the verified upload_file() behaviour.

Finalize_sandbox_task.description: Step 3 of 3. Task id goes in the query string, community in the JSON body.

Reset_sandbox_status.description: Starts this loop iteration's polling clean. InitializeVariable cannot live here (Logic Apps only allows it at the top level of the workflow) - sandboxStatus is initialized once at the top of the workflow and reset to the real starting value here on every iteration.

Set_sandbox_status.description: HTTP 204 with an empty body means PolySwarm has no such task (not found). It is handled explicitly as NOT_FOUND, which ends the poll loop, and the empty body is never read.

Compose_next_sandbox_status.description: Computes the next value of sandboxStatus. Logic Apps does not allow a variable to be set from an expression that reads the same variable.

Build_summary.description: Builds the summary used for both the incident comment and the PolySwarmSandbox_CL row, from the last poll of the sandbox task. The score is on the 0 to 10 scale both sandbox providers use. Verdict rule, used everywhere: KNOWN_GOOD is 'known good'; no score is 'unknown' (this covers a failed task and a timeout); at or above MaliciousScoreThreshold is 'malicious'; at or above SuspiciousScoreThreshold is 'suspicious'; otherwise 'benign'.

Determine_outcome.description: Outcome category, used only to choose the incident comment's narrative text - the verdict value itself (Build_summary?['verdict']) is the same single rule in every branch and in the PolySwarmSandbox_CL row.

Send_to_PolySwarmSandbox_CL.description: Logs Ingestion API: one row per detonation attempt, keyed by TaskId. CompletedAt is this playbook's own observed-terminal timestamp (utcNow()) - the verified SandboxTask response shape has no server-provided completion time.

metadata.title: PolySwarm - Sandbox Storage Blob Detonation - Incident Triggered
metadata.description: For every File entity on a Microsoft Sentinel incident, reads the matching blob from a fixed Azure Storage container and detonates it in the PolySwarm sandbox (CAPE or Triage), polling until complete or timeout and commenting verdict, score, malware family, MITRE ATT&CK techniques and a report link back to the incident. Defaults to your private PolySwarm community; refuses to submit to the public community unless AllowPublicCommunity is explicitly set. Never creates an incident. See the template's postDeployment notes for how this differs from the Recorded Future / Google reference playbooks it is modelled on.
prerequisites: A PolySwarm API key with sandbox access, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault.
The private PolySwarm community you want detonations to land in.
An Azure Storage account and container that already holds the files referenced by incident File entities (for example, files an upstream evidence-capture step has placed there).

The PolySwarmSandbox_CL Data Collection Endpoint and Data Collection Rule deployed (Data Connectors folder - not owned by this playbook). This playbook is the only writer to that table: it POSTs one row per detonation attempt (including timeouts) via the Logs Ingestion API, since PolySwarm's own sandbox task list API does not carry verdicts.
postDeployment: 1. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's system-assigned managed identity.
2. Assign the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault (named by the KeyVaultName parameter) to the same managed identity.
3. Assign the 'Storage Blob Data Reader' role on the Storage Account (named by StorageAccountName) to the same managed identity.

4. The 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' role on the Data Collection Rule (DcrResourceId) is assigned automatically at deployment when create_role_assignment is true (default) and the deploying principal can grant RBAC roles on that DCR; otherwise set create_role_assignment to false and assign the role manually.
5. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel, Azure Key Vault and Azure Blob Storage API connections if they show as unauthorized.
6. Attach the playbook to an automation rule so it runs on incidents with a File entity, or run it manually.

metadata.title: PolySwarm - Sandbox URL Detonation - Entity Triggered
metadata.description: Entity-trigger variant of PolySwarm-Sandbox-Url. An analyst runs this directly from a Url entity on an incident (Sentinel entity blade 'Run playbook'), rather than on the whole incident. Same sandbox flow, Key Vault key, community guard and incident comment as the incident-triggered variant. Refuses to submit private, loopback, link-local, reserved, single-label and IPv6 hosts, and non-http(s) schemes: a URL that points at an internal address would disclose internal host names to a third party. DNS names that resolve to private addresses are not detected (no resolver in Logic Apps).
prerequisites: A PolySwarm API key with sandbox access, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault.

The private PolySwarm community you want detonations to land in. Get one at https://polyswarm.network/account/api-keys; ask PolySwarm Customer Success for a private community if you do not have one yet.

The PolySwarmSandbox_CL Data Collection Endpoint and Data Collection Rule deployed (Data Connectors folder - not owned by this playbook). This playbook is the only writer to that table: it POSTs one row per detonation attempt (including timeouts) via the Logs Ingestion API, since PolySwarm's own sandbox task list API does not carry verdicts.
postDeployment: 1. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's system-assigned managed identity.
2. Assign the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault (named by the KeyVaultName parameter) to the same managed identity.

3. The 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' role on the Data Collection Rule (DcrResourceId) is assigned automatically at deployment when create_role_assignment is true (default) and the deploying principal can grant RBAC roles on that DCR; otherwise set create_role_assignment to false and assign the role manually.
4. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel and Azure Key Vault API connections if they show as unauthorized.

5. From an incident's entity blade, select a Url entity and choose 'Run playbook' to invoke this directly. Not attached via an automation rule (Sentinel entity triggers are analyst-invoked, not automation-rule-invoked).

Create_sandbox_task.description: Step 1 of 3. artifact_name is the URL itself - verified live, the URL string is also what gets uploaded as the artifact bytes in step 2 (a URL detonation does not fetch content client-side; PolySwarm's sandbox VM does the fetch).

Upload_artifact_bytes.description: Step 2 of 3. Uploads the URL string itself as the artifact bytes (verified live) - not fetched page content.

Finalize_sandbox_task.description: Step 3 of 3. Task id goes in the query string, community in the JSON body.

Reset_sandbox_status.description: Starts this loop iteration's polling clean. InitializeVariable cannot live here (Logic Apps only allows it at the top level of the workflow) - sandboxStatus is initialized once at the top of the workflow and reset to the real starting value here on every iteration.

Set_sandbox_status.description: HTTP 204 with an empty body means PolySwarm has no such task (not found). It is handled explicitly as NOT_FOUND, which ends the poll loop, and the empty body is never read.

Compose_next_sandbox_status.description: Computes the next value of sandboxStatus. Logic Apps does not allow a variable to be set from an expression that reads the same variable.

Build_summary.description: Builds the summary used for both the incident comment and the PolySwarmSandbox_CL row, from the last poll of the sandbox task. The score is on the 0 to 10 scale both sandbox providers use. Verdict rule, used everywhere: KNOWN_GOOD is 'known good'; no score is 'unknown' (this covers a failed task and a timeout); at or above MaliciousScoreThreshold is 'malicious'; at or above SuspiciousScoreThreshold is 'suspicious'; otherwise 'benign'.

Determine_outcome.description: Outcome category, used only to choose the incident comment's narrative text - the verdict value itself (Build_summary?['verdict']) is the same single rule in every branch and in the PolySwarmSandbox_CL row.

Send_to_PolySwarmSandbox_CL.description: Logs Ingestion API: one row per detonation attempt, keyed by TaskId. CompletedAt is this playbook's own observed-terminal timestamp (utcNow()) - the verified SandboxTask response shape has no server-provided completion time.

metadata.description: Detonates every URL entity on a Microsoft Sentinel incident in the PolySwarm sandbox (CAPE or Triage), polls until the task completes or times out, and writes verdict, score, malware family, MITRE ATT&CK techniques and a report link back to the incident as a comment. Defaults to your private PolySwarm community; refuses to submit to the public community unless AllowPublicCommunity is explicitly set. Never creates an incident. Refuses to submit private, loopback, link-local, reserved, single-label and IPv6 hosts, and non-http(s) schemes: a URL that points at an internal address would disclose internal host names to a third party. DNS names that resolve to private addresses are not detected (no resolver in Logic Apps).
prerequisites: A PolySwarm API key with sandbox access, stored as a secret in an Azure Key Vault.

The private PolySwarm community you want detonations to land in. Get one at https://polyswarm.network/account/api-keys; ask PolySwarm Customer Success for a private community if you do not have one yet.

The PolySwarmSandbox_CL Data Collection Endpoint and Data Collection Rule deployed (Data Connectors folder - not owned by this playbook). This playbook is the only writer to that table: it POSTs one row per detonation attempt (including timeouts) via the Logs Ingestion API, since PolySwarm's own sandbox task list API does not carry verdicts.
postDeployment: 1. Assign the 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' role on the resource group (or workspace) to this playbook's system-assigned managed identity.
2. Assign the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role on the Key Vault (named by the KeyVaultName parameter) to the same managed identity.

3. The 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' role on the Data Collection Rule (DcrResourceId) is assigned automatically at deployment when create_role_assignment is true (default) and the deploying principal can grant RBAC roles on that DCR; otherwise set create_role_assignment to false and assign the role manually.
4. Authorize the Microsoft Sentinel and Azure Key Vault API connections if they show as unauthorized.

5. Attach the playbook to an automation rule (or run it manually from an incident) so it runs on incidents with a Url entity. Consider gating the automation rule to only run on analyst request, given sandbox detonation is metered and takes minutes, not seconds.

Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

PolySwarm is a threat intelligence platform built on a marketplace of competing detection engines. Files, URLs, IP addresses and domains are analyzed by multiple engines in parallel, their consensus is scored as a single PolyScore, PolyUnite identifies the malware family, and sandbox detonation adds behavioral analysis. This solution enriches Microsoft Sentinel incident entities (file hashes, URLs, IP addresses and domains) with PolySwarm's multi-engine malware verdicts, naming every engine that agreed, and lets an analyst detonate a URL, an email attachment, an Azure Storage blob, or a file retrieved directly from a device through Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, in the PolySwarm sandbox, returning a score-derived verdict, malware family, MITRE ATT&CK techniques and a report link on the incident. Data connectors bring PolySwarm threat intelligence, from an organization's own PolySwarm hunt results and from the PolySwarm curated feed, into Microsoft Sentinel's native threat intelligence table, so Microsoft's built-in indicator matching runs against PolySwarm data alongside the analytics rules and hunting queries this solution provides.

Coverage by indicator type: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, URL, domain and IP are answered. Email addresses are not supported, because PolySwarm has no endpoint for them. A small PolySwarm status workbook shows what has arrived from each connector, reading only your own workspace.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used: This solution depends on underlying Microsoft technologies. Some of these dependencies either may be in Preview state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs:

  • Logic Apps
  • Microsoft Sentinel Codeless Connector Framework
  • Threat Indicators
  • Key Vault
